newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia against U.S. plan to cut phone rates.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia against U.S. plan to cut phone rates.

text.p: Malaysia opposes a U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) proposal for lower international telephone settlement rates, Malaysian Energy, Telecommunications and Posts minister said on Thursday.
Leo Moggie said: "I think in general, we do not agree with the way the FCC has tried to put unilaterally a benchmark in the accounting rate."
The U.S. body recently proposed a ceiling rate for U.S telephone companies carrying U.S. phone calls in other countries or territories.

Analysts have said this will mean significantly lower international telephone settlement rates, and would have a large impact on most Asian telephone companies, which generally pay higher U.S. settlement rates than their counterparts in other parts of the world.
Moggie told reporters at a telecommunications function on Thursday that there should be discussions between the FCC and regional telecommunications companies on the issue.
"My own feeling is that a number of countries are also not in agreement. We are not saying that there is no merit in the accounting system, but it should be subject to discussion," the minister said.
He said that his ministry had found from talking with telecommunications firms in the region that they also disagree with the FCC's proposal.
